Investigators linked a 2025 Central Harlem outbreak to cooling tower systems contaminated with Legionella bacteria. The outbreak included 118 confirmed cases, 92 hospitalizations, and 7 deaths. Patients were older on average, with a median age of 65, and many became sick enough to need hospital care. The twist: genetic testing pointed to two cooling tower systems on the same block. The lesson is uncomfortable but clear: public health often depends on infrastructure most people never see.
